pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome To Lyndhurst School | Independent School in Surrey
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Lyndhurst School
Lyndhurst is a small, family-run independent prep school for children aged 3-11 in Camberley, Surrey.
The best way to truly feel our ethos is to visit us; soak up the atmosphere for yourself and meet the children and staff who make up our warm and incredibly special community.
Headmistress’s Welcome
For over 130 years, Lyndhurst has been a special part of the Camberley community, and it is this strong sense of community that continues to make our school such a wonderful place to learn and grow.
We are a small, friendly school where every child is known and valued as an individual. We want our children to feel happy, supported and confident, while being encouraged to discover their interests, develop their talents and always give their best.
At Lyndhurst, we believe that education is about more than academic success. It is about nurturing curiosity, kindness, confidence and a lifelong love of learning. Our children are encouraged to get involved and make the most of every opportunity, both inside and outside the classroom. I am incredibly proud of the warm and supportive community we have at Lyndhurst, and I look forward to continuing to work closely with our children, families and staff to ensure that every child feels that they belong and has the opportunity to flourish.
Early Years Little Lyndhurst incorporates Pre-Reception and Reception classes under the one roof. Early Years Pre-Prep In Reception, Year 1 and 2 you will find children participating in ‘hands-on’, practical activities which will lead to meaningful and exciting cross-curricular links. Pre-Prep Prep The Prep department of Lyndhurst consists of Years 3 to 6. Prep
Endorsements from Destination Schools
We have worked well with Lyndhurst School for well over a decade and recognise how well prepared the pupils who transition to Salesian College are. These young men have consistently demonstrated exceptional social and academic development in Lyndhurst, which has equipped them to adapt seamlessly to their new environment.
At Lyndhurst, they have been nurtured to become happy, well-rounded individuals. Their ability to integrate and thrive at Salesian College is a testament to the strong foundation laid during their primary years. These students not only excel academically but also embody the values of respect, resilience, and responsibility.
The pupils that have joined Luckley House from Lyndhurst School are a remarkable group, showcasing dedication and passion across a variety of activities. Several have demonstrated a strong commitment to the theatre arts, excelling in their work and pushing themselves to reach their full potential. Their ability to make new friends and contribute positively to the classroom environment is truly commendable.
Others, like one pupil involved in the CCF, have thrived through extracurricular experiences, displaying growth and enthusiasm in both expeditions and sports. Regularly representing the school in football, rugby, and cricket, these pupils develop valuable skills that benefit them not only in sports but also in their academic pursuits. Overall, they embody the spirit of dedication, teamwork, and excellence.
Endorsements from Parents
I consider putting my children into Lyndhurst as one of the best decisions I have ever made. The school is not elitist, genuinely takes children of all levels of ability, and then make it so no one sees the difference. All children are celebrated, all children achieve to their highest ability. The teachers there are the kind of people who genuinely love their jobs – everyone at the school is passionately committed to your children, led by an outstanding head master who is extremely involved with each child and values building emotional intelligence as highly as academic achievements. The range of subjects, activities and experience is unrivalled. All the children partake in sports, shows, play a musical instrument, the wrap around care is educational as well as fun. Neither of my children, have ever, in the last four years at Lyndhurst said they didn’t want to go to school today, I know that the start Lyndhurst has given them will set them up for life and as a parent I am eternally grateful.
Our three-year-old has settled in wonderfully and loves the school. The teachers and assistants are well organised, friendly, and create an excellent learning environment. The schedules are varied with plenty of opportunities for outdoor playing and learning. My wife and I also love the proximity to the prep school and the interactions the nursery can have with bigger kids especially during after school. The 8am to 6pm care is very convenient for two working parents.
A fantastic school! My son is now into his second year at Lyndhurst (reception) and it is one of the best decisions that we have made for him (and us). The school’s before and after care is second-to-none, and along with the wonderful teachers and staff means that my son very much enjoys his school day. His academic progress has been rapid, and he has access to a very wide variety of sports and extra-curricular activities. It has been an excellent choice of school.

pageCache.pageTitle: History | Nursery In Surrey | Lyndhurst School
pageCache.text:
History
Welcome to Lyndhurst School: Inspiring Young Minds Since 1895
Founded in 1895, Lyndhurst School is one of the few preparatory schools in the region with an unbroken history spanning over a century. Our commitment to educating the whole child lies at the heart of everything we do.
We pride ourselves on being a small, friendly school with a warm, family-oriented atmosphere. Our holistic approach to education nurtures academic excellence, personal growth, and a love of learning that stays with pupils for life.
Tailored Learning, Exceptional Outcomes With small class sizes, our dedicated teachers get to know each pupil, tailoring the curriculum to meet individual needs while fostering collaboration and peer learning. This balance creates a dynamic, supportive, and intellectually challenging environment.
Our reputation for high academic achievement is matched by excellent examination results. Every year, our pupils secure places at leading senior schools, often earning scholarships in academics, sports, music, and art.
A Rich and Diverse Curriculum Beyond the classroom, we offer a wealth of opportunities for pupils to develop their talents. We make full use of excellent local sporting facilities, including weekly swimming lessons and a variety of sports activities.
Modern Foreign Languages are integrated throughout the school, broadening pupils’ cultural horizons.
A Creative and Expressive Arts Culture Music and Drama are central to our school life. With two choirs and an orchestra, we foster a love for performance and creative expression. Our pupils also achieve remarkable success in Associated Board of Music examinations.
Lyndhurst School is a place where children thrive, learn, and grow — academically, socially, and creatively. We invite you to discover the warmth and excellence that set our school apart.

pageCache.pageTitle: Safeguarding | Nursery in Camberley | Lyndhurst School
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility
Safeguarding is the protection of children from harm and ensuring they grow up in a safe and caring environment.
Lyndhurst School recognises its moral and statutory responsibility to safeguard and promote the welfare of all pupils. We endeavour to provide a safe and welcoming environment where children are respected and valued. We are alert to the signs of abuse and neglect and operate within Surrey’s agreed inter-agency procedures to ensure that children receive effective support, protection and justice. Child protection forms part of the school’s safeguarding responsibilities.
Lyndhurst School 25 26 Safeguarding Policy
Concerns regarding the welfare of a child can be raised with a member of the Lyndhurst Safeguarding Team:
Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL)
Miss Emma Morgan (Headmistress)
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads
Miss Charlotte Goswell (Early Years Lead)
Governor responsible for Safeguarding
Jo Atkins (School Governor)
To contact our safeguarding team, please use: dsl@lyndhurstschool.co.uk
Surrey Children’s Single Point of Access (C-SPA)
Telephone: 03004709100
Email: cspa@surreycc.gov.uk
Signing In
Lyndhurst School is committed to the highest standards in protecting and safeguarding the children entrusted to our care. You will be asked to sign in and wear a visitor’s badge when you come to visit the school.
A red lanyard means you will have to be accompanied whilst on the school premises.
A green lanyard indicates that the visitor has completed DBS checks, however, is not directly employed by the school.
Please remember to sign out and return your lanyard to the Front Office before leaving the premises.
Daily Collection

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum | Private School in Surrey | Lyndhurst School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
To learn more about our curriculum, please click on the subjects below
Art & DT
Art & DT
Our vibrant Art and Design Technology space inspires creativity and self-expression. Pupils of all year groups enjoy weekly lessons, working on diverse projects ranging from glove puppets to mosaics and pottery.
They explore techniques inspired by significant artists, fostering confidence in their creative abilities. Through our Design and Technology curriculum, pupils develop critical thinking skills, learn to take risks, and confidently evaluate and improve their work.
Computing & IT
Computing & IT
We equip pupils with essential technological skills, fostering confidence and a solid understanding of how computers work. Technology is presented as a powerful tool for learning, innovation, and discovery.
E-Safety is a key focus from Pre-Reception, with age-appropriate lessons, interactive workshops, and whole-school events teaching children how to stay safe online. Programming and coding are integral parts of the curriculum, allowing pupils to explore various programming languages through engaging activities and topics.
Media
Media
Our award-winning Media Club, led by former international news journalist Miss Joyce, inspires pupils to become confident storytellers and critical thinkers. Open to Years 3 to 6, the club creates multimedia content, including our much-anticipated annual school newspaper, Lyndhurst World.
We were especially proud of the Year 5 team’s Climate Crew podcast, which won the Learn2Think Foundation’s Young Journalist of the Year 2021 award. Judges praised their teamwork, professionalism, and interviewing skills.
Media Club encourages pupils to uncover stories within our school, conduct interviews, and develop key skills in journalism, communication, teamwork, and writing. More importantly, it empowers them to share their voices, fostering confidence and a belief in their ability to create meaningful change.
English
English
Our English curriculum empowers children to express their ideas fluently, confidently, and creatively in both speech and writing.
Early reading and phonics are a top priority, with all pupils following the Read Write Inc. Phonics programme to build strong foundational reading and writing skills. Each term, immersive themes inspire purposeful reading and writing across the curriculum.
We enrich pupils’ learning with visits from celebrated poets, authors, and theatre companies. Whole-school competitions in public speaking, creative writing, spelling, and reading challenge pupils to excel.
To support individual progress, every pupil has access to DoodleEnglish and DoodleSpell, providing personalized learning experiences that strengthen classroom learning.
Our approach equips pupils with vital English skills, preparing them for lifelong success.
Humanities
Humanities
Humanities at Lyndhurst encompasses History and Geography, fostering curiosity about the world and its past.
In History, pupils explore how past events have shaped the present, gaining knowledge of key dates and events. Geography encourages children to think beyond the classroom, develop a sense of identity, and understand their place in the local and global context.
Role play, dressing up, and immersive themed days bring learning to life, while educational trips provide hands-on experiences of the people, places, and cultures they study.
Maths
Maths
At Lyndhurst, we believe Maths should be enjoyed, not feared. From the start of their journey with us, pupils are encouraged to approach Maths with curiosity and confidence.
Lessons are fun, engaging, and tailored to individual abilities, with hands-on practical activities alongside developing strong written skills, including the importance of showing working out (SWO). Our progressive curriculum ensures full topic coverage for a smooth transition to senior school.
Every child benefits from DoodleMaths and DoodleTables, personalized platforms that support and stretch learning as needed. Pupils also showcase their skills through competitions such as the Primary Maths and First Mathematics Challenges, local school events, and our annual immersive Maths Day.
Languages
Languages
We believe language learning should be engaging and fun. French is taught throughout the school, with Year 6 also exploring Spanish. Additionally, our Spanish Clubs cater to pupils from Reception to Year 6.
Language learning begins in Pre-Reception with playful activities focused on listening and speaking. As pupils progress, reading and writing skills are developed through varied materials and interactive games. Lessons are tailored to ensure all children are supported or challenged appropriately.
Our goal is to foster a love for languages and an appreciation for diverse cultures, inspiring pupils to connect with the wider world.
Outdoor Learning
Outdoor Learning
Outdoor learning is a vital part of life at Lyndhurst School. LEAF lessons connect children with nature, using our school grounds and local natural spaces for exploration and discovery.
Pupils develop bushcraft skills such as fire-starting with flint and steel, whittling, carving, and knot tying to build dens. Pre-Prep and Little Lyndhurst have weekly sessions, while Prep pupils enjoy dedicated whole afternoons each half term.
LEAF fosters hands-on learning, adventure, and a deeper appreciation for the natural world.
Drama
Drama
Drama at Lyndhurst nurtures self-confidence, communication, and creativity while developing performance skills and teamwork.
Taught by a specialist teacher, pupils explore characterisation, voice projection, expression, and body language. They devise narratives and bring them to life through engaging performances.
Each year, children participate in plays, assemblies, and drama festivals, with Lyndhurst recently winning Best Musical Theatre Production at the ISA Drama Competition. Regular workshops with professional actors further enrich their skills, laying strong foundations for future drama studies.
LAMDA
LAMDA
LAMDA (London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art) exams are the speech and drama equivalent of music grades, fostering vocal, physical, and interpretive skills.
Through preparation for Acting Exams, pupils explore dramatic texts, develop authentic performances, and build confidence, presence, and strong speaking skills.
As a registered LAMDA examination centre, Lyndhurst provides pupils with valuable qualifications recognized on the Regulated Qualifications Framework, enhancing their future prospects.
PSHCE
PSHCE
PSHCE at Lyndhurst equips children with the knowledge, skills, and values needed to thrive in a 21st-century society. Topics are explored through six key themes: ‘Being Me in My World,’ ‘Celebrating Differences,’ ‘Dreams & Goals,’ ‘Healthy Me,’ ‘Relationships,’ and ‘Changing Me.’ These themes cover everything from global sustainability to first aid, mindfulness, and mental wellbeing.
Our curriculum fosters self-belief, kindness, respect, and resilience, empowering pupils to develop strong decision-making skills and engage with their school and local community. The School Council, made up of pupils from Reception to Year 6, actively contributes ideas to improve the school, ensuring every voice is heard.
STEM
STEM
STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Maths) is an exciting and integral part of life at Lyndhurst, designed to challenge and stimulate curiosity.
Our broad, progressive curriculum starts with exploring the immediate world and senses, nurturing children’s inquisitive minds through hands-on experiments and investigations. We connect learning to real-world events, encouraging pupils to engage with current issues. The Eco-Council, made up of students, actively debates environmental topics and fosters a passion for the world around them.
RE
RE
Religious Education at Lyndhurst provides children with opportunities to ask questions, explore ideas, and reflect on right and wrong in a supportive environment. We teach the universal principles shared by all faiths, such as the golden rule of treating others as we wish to be treated.
As a non-denominational school with a Christian ethos, we embrace a multicultural community and promote mutual respect. Pupils learn about major world religions and are encouraged to show compassion and respect for others’ beliefs.
Lyndhurst families are invited to share their experiences, and we celebrate festivals like Diwali, Easter, and Chinese New Year. We also have strong ties with St. Michael’s Church, where we celebrate our Christmas Carol Service.
Sport
Sport
At Lyndhurst, Physical Education is key to developing the whole child—academically, socially, emotionally, spiritually, and physically. PE fosters self-esteem, confidence, and character traits such as perseverance, resilience, teamwork, and leadership.
We offer a broad range of sporting opportunities through both the curriculum and extracurricular clubs, ensuring all children, regardless of ability, can participate in individual and team sports. From Year 3, pupils compete in house fixtures and local prep school competitions.
Our annual Sports Day at Aldershot Military Stadium is a highlight, with pupils representing their houses in a day of track and field events. Swimming is also a key part of our programme, with lessons for all children from Reception to Year 6.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum Plus | Independent School in Surrey | Lyndhurst School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Plus
The curriculum is the interaction between the teacher and the learner and, as such transmits attitudes and values, in addition to knowledge, skills and understanding. The Directors, Governors and staff of Lyndhurst School will create high standards through high expectations, which are at the core of the attitudes and values transmitted through our curriculum delivery. The school ensures that children have a range of learning experiences that challenge, stimulate and promote thinking and learning.
At Lyndhurst we pride ourselves on providing an education that is rich in linguistic, mathematical, scientific, technological, human and social, physical, and aesthetic and creative experiences. To consolidate the learnings the children, have as part of their curriculum, we offer a wide range of carefully planned enrichment activities each term. These activities support the curriculum to promote a positive attitude towards learning, so that pupils enjoy coming to school and acquire a solid base for lifelong learning. We use the best of the National Curriculum and then enhance it so it becomes more skills based, we like to think of it as National Curriculum plus.
By the end of Year 5, the key elements of Eleven Plus entrance have been covered and are consolidated in the first term of Year 6, ready for sitting entrance exams.

Reception Class (Ages 4-5) Our Reception class offers a seamless transition from the Early Years Foundation Stage to formal schooling. Located alongside the Year 1 classroom, it features two dedicated outdoor areas where children thrive through play-based learning and engaging adult-led activities.
With a creative and stimulating curriculum, we encourage outdoor exploration, nature-based activities, and exercise to develop confident, curious learners. Reception children benefit from specialist lessons in Sport, Dance, Music, and French, as well as weekly swimming sessions at the local leisure centre.
Strong links with Nursery and Year 1 ensure a smooth educational journey, preparing children to confidently embrace the next step in their learning adventure

pageCache.pageTitle: Pre-prep | Nursery in Surrey | Lyndhurst School
pageCache.text:
Pre-Prep
The Pre-Prep department at Lyndhurst School consists of Year 1 and 2. We pride ourselves on our smaller inclusive class sizes. Each day in the life of a five, six- and seven-year-olds promises the discovery of new skills, expansion of knowledge and a variety of new experiences. All learning takes place in a supportive and nurturing environment which enables children to develop their self-confidence and self-esteem.
In Year 1, we lay the foundation for lifelong learning by fostering curiosity, creativity, and a love for discovery. Our focus is on developing essential skills in reading, writing, and mathematics through engaging, hands-on activities tailored to each child’s needs.
Year 2 is an exciting time of growth, where children continue to build upon their core skills with growing confidence and enthusiasm. We place a strong focus on advancing reading, spelling, and handwriting, alongside deepening mathematical understanding through engaging lessons and problem-solving activities.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pre-School | Independent School in Surrey | Lyndhurst School
pageCache.text:
Pre-Reception
The youngest in our school begin their exciting journey with us when they join us in our Pre-Reception.
Through our high adult to child ratio and our warm, family atmosphere, children settle into our sensitive and nurturing environment as if they have always been part of the Lyndhurst family.
We celebrate every child’s strengths, encouraging them to follow their interests, to explore, investigate, question and learn. Children enjoy a varied timetable with access to all main school facilities.
Our Pre-Reception children have daily phonics and maths sessions, specialist lessons in PE, French, drama, dance, outdoor learning and music whilst still having plenty of opportunities to play, explore and develop their own learning and interests both inside and outside of the classroom.
Our plentiful outside space offers many opportunities for outside learning, exploration and play to take place. Our activities are fun, engaging, promoting confidence and independence.
Regular external visitors are always welcome to the school to help to open up the world for the children and we have exciting trips out during the year to a wide range of local places of interest.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prep | Private School in Surrey | Lyndhurst School
pageCache.text:
Prep
Year 3
Year 3 marks the exciting beginning of Prep School, where children embark on the next chapter of their educational journey. At this stage, they begin learning Maths and English with specialist teachers, fostering a deeper understanding and enthusiasm for these core subjects.
Beyond the classroom, Year 3 offers enriching experiences, including a trip to a local activity centre. This adventure helps build independence, teamwork, and confidence. Additionally, Year 3 pupils take part in a collaborative Drama project alongside Year 5, allowing them to develop creativity, communication skills, and a love for performance.
This year is a fantastic blend of academic progression and hands-on experiences, laying a strong foundation for the years ahead.
Year 4
In Year 4, children are encouraged to become more independent and responsible, both in their learning and in managing their belongings. They begin to take greater ownership of their studies, fostering self-discipline and organisational skills.
Throughout the year, the workload gradually increases to help them build resilience and develop effective study habits. By the end of Year 4, children are well-prepared to meet the challenges of the next stage in their educational journey, laying a solid foundation for working towards senior school exams.
Year 4 is all about growing independence, building confidence, and embracing new responsibilities.
Year 5
Year 5 is a pivotal stage in your child’s academic journey, with the primary focus on preparing for senior school exams. Our dedicated teachers provide the guidance and support needed to help pupils build confidence, develop effective study habits, and reach their full academic potential.
However, at Lyndhurst, we believe in educating the whole child. Alongside academic preparation, there are plenty of opportunities for children to explore and develop their creative and sporting talents. Whether through drama, music, art, or sports, every child is encouraged to discover their passions and grow holistically.
Additionally, Year 5 pupils enjoy a short residential break at a local activity centre, fostering independence, teamwork, and a sense of adventure.
Year 5 is a year of growth, challenge, and exciting new experiences, ensuring each pupil is fully prepared for the next stage of their educational journey.
Year 6
Year 6 is a transformative and rewarding year, beginning with the final push towards senior school exams and culminating in a celebration of each child’s personal and academic journey. Our goal is to ensure that every pupil feels prepared, confident, and ready for the challenges ahead.
Beyond academics, Year 6 offers exciting opportunities for personal growth, including a five-day residential trip where pupils explore new adventures, build resilience, and strengthen friendships.
By the end of Year 6, our aim is for every child to leave Lyndhurst as a well-rounded, self-confident, and independent individual, equipped with the skills, knowledge, and mindset necessary to thrive in the next stage of their education and beyond.
We proudly offer residential trips in Years 5 and 6. These larger trips allow our children to further build their resilience and independence, over a number of nights away from home. Year 5 are fortunate enough to spend time in an outdoor activity centre, where they take part in climbing, kayaking and caving. Year 6 spend an entire week in the Brecon Beacons, enjoying the Welsh countryside where they raft build, take aim in archery and practise their orienteering skills. Residentials are an important part of the Lyndhurst ethos, as we ensure they are as inspiring and engaging as possible.

Destination Schools
As a non-selective school, we take great pride in the success of our pupils, ensuring each child fulfils their potential during their time at Lyndhurst. We are committed to helping families find the right senior school, with 100% of our leavers securing places at their chosen schools.
In Year 6, children are fully prepared for entrance and scholarship requirements, with an expectation that all pupils complete their full seven-year journey at Lyndhurst.
From the start of Year 5, we provide guidance on ‘Future Schools,’ beginning with an information session for parents. Ongoing meetings with senior staff ensure families feel supported in making informed choices.
Our leavers have successfully joined top schools, including Farnborough Hill, Salesian College, Luckley House, Holme Grange, LVS Ascot, St Nicholas, Tomlinscote, Collingwood, and Kings International—many achieving academic scholarships. We are dedicated to supporting you and your child every step of the way.

Preparatory School Years
Preparatory education at Lyndhurst School lays the foundation for academic success, personal growth, and lifelong learning. Our nurturing environment supports children as they develop independence, confidence, and a love for learning.
With a broad and engaging curriculum, specialist teaching, and a focus on both academic excellence and personal development, we ensure every child reaches their full potential. Beyond the classroom, pupils benefit from enriching experiences in the arts, sports, and outdoor learning, fostering creativity, teamwork, and resilience.
At Lyndhurst, we are committed to preparing our pupils for a smooth transition to senior school, equipping them with the knowledge, skills, and values needed to thrive in the next stage of their educational journey.
